steps.cap: A slice through one spot on a wafer, magnified until its layers show.
A film a few atoms thick is laid over the whole wafer.
A light-sensitive coating, the resist, is spun on top.
Light shines through a stencil and changes the resist wherever it lands.
A wash removes the resist the light reached, leaving the stencil’s pattern.
A plasma cuts straight down through the film wherever the resist is gone.
The leftover resist is removed. The pattern now sits in the film.
Insulator fills the gaps and the next layer goes on. A chip takes more than a thousand of these rounds.
